Question: The total area of all the faces of a rectangular solid is \(22\text{ cm}^2,\) and the total length of all its edges is \(24\text{ cm}.\) Then the length in cm of any one of its internal diagonals is
Solution:
Let the three positive dimensions, measured in centimeters, be \(u,v,w\). There are four edges of each length and two faces of each of the three area types. Therefore
\[
4(u+v+w)=24,\qquad 2(uv+uw+vw)=22,
\]
so
\[
u+v+w=6,\qquad uv+uw+vw=11.
\]

We need the squares of the dimensions for the diagonal. Squaring their sum brings together exactly the quantities given:
\[
\begin{aligned}
u^2+v^2+w^2
&=(u+v+w)^2-2(uv+uw+vw)\\
&=6^2-2(11)=14.
\end{aligned}
\]

By the Pythagorean theorem, a face diagonal has squared length \(u^2+v^2\). That face diagonal and a perpendicular edge of length \(w\) form a right triangle whose hypotenuse is an internal diagonal. Thus every internal diagonal has squared length \(u^2+v^2+w^2=14\), and its length is \(\boxed{\sqrt{14}\text{ cm}}\), choice D.
